exposure: intended vaginal breech birth (unsuccessful, leading to secondary cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 3172 singleton breech presentations beyond 36 weeks gestation at a German tertiary perinatal center over 21 years.
finding: Vaginal breech birth was associated with fewer maternal complications but elevated short-term neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Compared to planned cesarean section, intended vaginal breech birth was associated with significantly lower maternal blood loss and shorter hospital stays, but also significantly more frequent neonatal interventions and increased short-term neonatal morbidity.
